_meta.title: Value Compass — evidence classification
_meta.what_this_is: A derived layer. It adds no facts. For every recorded axis assessment it records what the written rationale rests on, which of its sources are about that maker, and whether the score may be shown or compared.
_meta.display_rule: Where our research record contains no finding for a maker on an axis, no score is shown. The recorded value is preserved and shown on request. We do not state that the maker published nothing — only that we have not established it.
_meta.eligibility_rule: One rule governs ordering, comparison markers, switching differences and any recommendation: the assessment must carry relevant, traceable support for the actual claim (a source about this maker that covers what the score rests on), and the assessment must be justified by that support. Confidence A or B alone is not sufficient. A single authoritative source can carry a narrow factual claim; the number of sources does not determine quality.

bases.sourced: Rationale points at something on record and cites a source about this maker.
bases.unsourced: Rationale points at something on record, but no source about this maker is attached.
bases.contextual: Rationale reasons from jurisdiction, company size or position in the stack, not from evidence about this maker.
bases.not_established: Our research has not established a finding for this maker on this axis.

claim_support.establishes_fact: The cited material directly establishes a narrow fact about this maker. The fact is preserved and displayed whether or not the axis score is eligible.
claim_support.partial: The cited material covers part of a multi-part rationale. Any narrow fact it does establish is preserved.
claim_support.unreviewed: A source about this maker is cited, but the fit between source and claim has not been reviewed.
claim_support.none: No source about this maker to review.

_meta.score_justification_rule: A narrow fact justifies a whole 0–4 axis score only under a scoring rule that exists in the rubric. Transparency has one (the FMTI anchor and its band mapping). No other axis does: each lists sub-indicators and states no rule for combining them, so evidence for one sub-indicator cannot settle the axis. We do not write a rule after the fact to keep a score eligible.
_meta.provenance_note: Every classification here is automated_provisional: produced by reading the recorded rationale against the rubric, not by a human re-reading the sources. None is marked human-reviewed.

relationship_types.controlling_stake: A stake the record describes as controlling.
relationship_types.equity_investment: Money invested for a stake. Not by itself control.
relationship_types.funding_commitment: Money announced or committed. Check the status field for whether it has been paid.
relationship_types.commercial_dependency: An investor who is also a supplier or customer of the maker.
relationship_types.passive_economic: Index-fund ownership of a public parent. Economic exposure, exercised through routine governance votes.
relationship_types.unspecified: This dataset records a backing relationship but not what kind.

relationship_statuses.completed: The record describes this as done.
relationship_statuses.announced: Announced. The record does not say it has closed.
relationship_statuses.pending: The record describes it as not yet closed.
relationship_statuses.contingent: Part or all of it depends on a future event.

absence_evidence_requirements.what_counts: A documented absence needs a source that examined the question, an explicit scope, and a date the coverage runs to. An authored false value is not evidence, and a scope sentence written by us describes a claim rather than supporting it.

attribution.self_report: The company states there is no such holder.
attribution.independent: A third party checked and found none.
